fp.note: Historically, the only thing standing between Kincaid and consistent TE1 production has been his route rate. Going forward, Kincaid is a set-and-forget TE1 until proven otherwise.

A couple of close calls meant it didn't show up in the box score, but DK Metcalf's role was excellent on Sunday. The veteran wideout racked up 194 air yards, the second most of any player in the league. He also ran more in-breaking routes than last year: 54% of his routes were in-breaking, up from just 34% in 2025. Meanwhile, the Steelers' offense as a whole was shockingly pass-happy. Put these facts together, and Metcalf should easily rebound from this relatively slow start going forward.

Don't sell low on Luther Burden, who still has massive upside. Kalif Raymond isn't suddenly the Bears' WR1. However, it is undeniably concerning that Burden posted just a 68% route participation rate against the Panthers. With Rome Odunze dealing with a calf injury, that was actually the highest among Chicago's WRs, but it's far lower than we normally expect from starting wideouts, which is legitimately concerning. While everyone else argues about Colston Loveland's donut, try to quietly sell Burden at his draft-day cost, which he should fall from at least a little given what we just saw.

Tucker Kraft posted just a 48% route participation rate on Sunday, running only five more routes than Jonnu Smith. If this had come out of nowhere, it would be time to panic. However, Kraft is coming off a torn ACL suffered last November. He himself said this offseason that the team's plan is to ease him into the season. Find another tight end to start until Kraft's role ramps up (hopefully sooner rather than later), but don't give up on the explosive young TE entirely.

news.title: Alec Pierce (heel) to attempt to rehab instead of undergoing surgery

fp.note: The Bears ran absolutely wild in Week 1, and Kyle Monangai was a huge part of it. The second-year back racked up nearly 20 half-PPR points, largely thanks to a massive 61-yard touchdown run. However, Monangai's role wasn't actually all that encouraging: He saw just a 36% RB rush share, with 10 carries to D'Andre Swift's 18 (Swift also saw all three of the team's goal-line attempts). Monangai did outpace his veteran counterpart in targets (two) and route rate (40%), but it's hard to imagine him ever being a consistently large part of this loaded Chicago passing offense. Unless he keeps ripping off huge runs and the Bears keep scoring 50 points a game, Monangai is likely to be an inconsistent, frustrating option in redraft leagues. If you can cash in on the big week and general Bears hype to trade him for weekly starter value, I'd do it.

But he was also on the field far more than we might have expected, ranking second to DeVonta Smith with a very respectable 85% route rate. Given Lemon's exciting prospect profile, those routes should turn into actual downfield targets sooner rather than later. Combine that with the easy-button usage he already saw, and we could have a solid weekly starter by the time the season really gets going.

The third-round rookie led the 49ers' backfield with 14 carries in their shocking upset down under on Thursday, and he looked good doing it. Kenneth Gainwell did see the team's only two short-yardage carries, but Irving took the lone tote within the 10-yard line (Sean Tucker was sidelined by injury, but reports indicate he isn't headed for much of a role even when healthy). Gainwell, whose receiving ability may have been overrated thanks to playing with Aaron Rodgers last season, saw just one target on a 33% route rate. Especially given Irving also passed the eye test with the juice he showed as a rookie, he's looking set to outperform his draft cost for the rest of the season.

fp.note: If you paid any attention to fantasy football discussions this offseason, you probably heard that Davante Adams' 2025 success was largely based on unique usage as the Rams' go-to goal-line offense. Although his numbers were otherwise down across the board, 14 touchdowns, 11 of which came from within the 10-yard line, carried his season. With this in mind, it's an absolutely massive red flag that Adams played just one of LA's nine snaps inside the 20-yard line in Melbourne. Nine snaps (only six of which were inside the 10) is a small sample, but given how TD-dependent Adams' profile is at this point, I'd recommend overreacting rather than underreacting to this change in usage.

Normally, I prefer buying high after Week 1 rather than attempting to buy low, which is usually easier said than done. But Jaylen Waddle's Denver debut was so bad — one catch for two yards on just three targets — that his early-round investors may already be panicking. Denver's offense looked terrible all around on Monday night, but Waddle still led the team with a respectable 79% route share. More importantly, I simply believe in his talent eventually winning out. If you do too, now is the time to send an offer.

MarShawn Lloyd played his second career NFL game on Sunday; it didn't go well. The 2024 third-rounder was outsnapped by Chris Brooks (37 to 30), who also led the backfield in routes (10 to seven). However, Lloyd did lead the backfield with 13 carries (Brooks saw seven). Former Steeler Kaleb Jonson did not play a snap. Green Bay's rushing offense should bounce back when not facing Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense. If there's upside to be found here while Josh Jacobs remains sidelined, it's Lloyd. Don't give up on him just yet.

Saquon averaged a 50% route participation rate in 2025, with a season-low mark of 27%. On Sunday, he tied that low, running nine routes while Will Shipley ran seven. Meanwhile, Barkley failed to find any room to run behind a Philadelphia offensive line that is a far cry from the top-tier unit that helped him dominate in 2024. Saquon's ADP this offseason was a bet on a bounce-back; one week in, that bounce-back doesn't look likely. If you can still cash in on his name brand for legit RB1 value, I'd do it.

fp.note: The Raiders won't get to play the Dolphins every week. But Ashton Jeanty's usage in Week 1 was excellent, including six targets for an elite 20% target share. With the preseason prayer circle firmly in the rearview mirror, Jeanty is a locked-in RB1 and a steal for anyone who got him at a discount thanks to his ankle injury.

Lemon recorded three catches NFL debut ... for negative five yards. The 20th-overall pick was used exclusively at the line of scrimmage against the Commanders, somehow posting a negative ADOT on his four targets. But he was also on the field far more than we might have expected, ranking second to DeVonta Smith with a very respectable 85% route rate. Given Lemon's exciting prospect profile, those routes should turn into actual downfield targets sooner rather than later. Combine that with the easy-button usage he already saw, and we could have a solid weekly starter by the time the season really gets going.

Given that he's on the Browns, it's hard to see how Denzel Boston's NFL debut could have gone better. He led the team in route share (90%), tied for the lead in target share (18%), and lapped the field in air yards share (58%). He finished with a solid fantasy day, too, although that was admittedly almost entirely thanks to a 46-yard touchdown in the smelliest of garbage time. There's a real chance Cleveland's overall ineptitude keeps Boston from ever emerging as a weekly starter, but I'll always recommend buying into a rookie flashing upside while they're still cheap.

Especially given that the Packers' offense actually posted a positive pass-rate over expectation — a huge departure from Matt LaFleur's usual tendencies — Golden is poised to dominate as long as this usage continues.

Antonio Williams isn't likely to be startable any time soon — he only ran 11 routes on Sunday. But he racked up four targets on those 11 routes, catching all four for 64 yards and a TD. I wouldn't actually pay anything with real value to acquire the third-round rookie, but he's a must-add. It's better to be early than late when a young player is flashing target-earning ability, especially when they're on a potentially exciting offense with non-elite competition.

news.title: Brock Bowers (knee) will practice this week
Caleb Williams (hamstring) labeled week-to-week with hamstring injury

fp.note: Saquon averaged a 50% route participation rate in 2025, with a season-low mark of 27%. On Sunday, he tied that low, running nine routes while Will Shipley ran seven. Meanwhile, Barkley failed to find any room to run behind a Philadelphia offensive line that is a far cry from the top-tier unit that helped him dominate in 2024. Saquon's ADP this offseason was a bet on a bounce-back; one week in, that bounce-back doesn't look likely. If you can still cash in on his name brand for legit RB1 value, I'd do it.

injury.comment: Barkley was seen on the sidelines holding his helmet after his first half injury and he did not return prior to halftime. Barkley took a carry in the third quarter and appears poised to return as the primary running back for the remainder of the game.

news.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) returns to the game

fp.note: Normally, I prefer buying high after Week 1 rather than attempting to buy low, which is usually easier said than done. But Jaylen Waddle's Denver debut was so bad — one catch for two yards on just three targets — that his early-round investors may already be panicking. Denver's offense looked terrible all around on Monday night, but Waddle still led the team with a respectable 79% route share. More importantly, I simply believe in his talent eventually winning out. If you do too, now is the time to send an offer.

Given that he's on the Browns, it's hard to see how Denzel Boston's NFL debut could have gone better. He led the team in route share (90%), tied for the lead in target share (18%), and lapped the field in air yards share (58%). He finished with a solid fantasy day, too, although that was admittedly almost entirely thanks to a 46-yard touchdown in the smelliest of garbage time. There's a real chance Cleveland's overall ineptitude keeps Boston from ever emerging as a weekly starter, but I'll always recommend buying into a rookie flashing upside while they're still cheap.

The third-round rookie led the 49ers' backfield with 14 carries in their shocking upset down under on Thursday, and he looked good doing it. It is worth noting that Christian McCaffrey was reportedly dealing with cramps during the contest — this isn't going to be a true timeshare any time soon. But Black's performance establishes him as at the very least one of the league's most valuable handcuffs, with potential to carve out standalone value a la Blake Corum. He should be rostered in every league.

news.title: Kaelon Black (groin) active for Week 2

injury.comment: The Jets are placing their first-round rookie on injured reserve after he suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut last week. He is going to miss at least four weeks as a result, but he's not expected to be out much beyond that. Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq will both see increased opportunities in his absence for the next few weeks at least.

news.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) placed on injured reserve

fp.note: MarShawn Lloyd played his second career NFL game on Sunday; it didn't go well. The 2024 third-rounder was outsnapped by Chris Brooks (37 to 30), who also led the backfield in routes (10 to seven). However, Lloyd did lead the backfield with 13 carries (Brooks saw seven). Former Steeler Kaleb Jonson did not play a snap. Green Bay's rushing offense should bounce back when not facing Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense. If there's upside to be found here while Josh Jacobs remains sidelined, it's Lloyd. Don't give up on him just yet.

news.title: Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for Week 2

fp.note: Rookie Kaelon Black leading the 49ers' backfield in carries obviously isn't what fantasy managers who spent a first-round pick on CMC wanted to see. But the veteran back was reportedly dealing with cramps; he still racked up his customary elite number of targets (eight). And, although his volume was lower, McCaffrey was actually more efficient on the ground and showed more juice in Week 1 than he did in 2025. Don't overreact to Black's usage — hold CMC and expect elite RB1 production to come.

Lemon recorded three catches NFL debut ... for negative five yards. The 20th-overall pick was used exclusively at the line of scrimmage against the Commanders, somehow posting a negative ADOT on his four targets. But he was also on the field far more than we might have expected, ranking second to DeVonta Smith with a very respectable 85% route rate. Given Lemon's exciting prospect profile, those routes should turn into actual downfield targets sooner rather than later. Combine that with the easy-button usage he already saw, and we could have a solid weekly starter by the time the season really gets going.

fp.note: Another player whose Week 1 role failed to live up to offseason hype, Gainwell saw just one target on a 33% route participation rate against the Bengals. Combined with just five carries, his role won't provide standalone value. If you can still sell him based on a draft-day cost that assumed some chance of that standalone value hitting, do it.

Don't sell low on Luther Burden, who still has massive upside. Kalif Raymond isn't suddenly the Bears' WR1. However, it is undeniably concerning that Burden posted just a 68% route participation rate against the Panthers. With Rome Odunze dealing with a calf injury, that was actually the highest among Chicago's WRs, but it's far lower than we normally expect from starting wideouts, which is legitimately concerning. While everyone else argues about Colston Loveland's donut, try to quietly sell Burden at his draft-day cost, which he should fall from at least a little given what we just saw.

Although he wasn't on the final injury report, Brooks dealt with a groin injury in the lead-up to the Panthers' season-opener. Especially given his injury history, it's not that surprising that he then proceeded to play just 13 snaps against the Bears. But the former second-round pick still managed to flash in his limited role, with a 48-yard reception down the sideline showing off the upside that tempted fantasy managers this offseason. Brooks might not be the Panthers' RB1 any time soon (or ever), but he's absolutely worth holding at least a few weeks longer.

fp.note: If Flowers didn't exit Week 1 early with a hamstring injury, it would already be too late to buy him. But that injury has perhaps opened one final window to acquire a guy who could be the story of the season. Flowers racked up five catches for 150 yards on just 11 routes on Sunday, absurd efficiency. He also hit pay dirt, already matching 20% of his total TD production from last season. This confirms my priors that Flowers is a truly elite talent who has just been unlucky on the touchdown front and is now primed for a monster year in Baltimore's new offense.
